title: the_wrong_house
beats: My delivery driver called me from outside a house that wasn't mine.
He read my address back. Every digit right. But he was standing across town.
The photo he sent showed my welcome mat. My door. My wind chimes. On a house I had never seen in my life.
I tipped him twenty bucks to leave the food and send me the pin.
Then I drove out there. Twenty minutes. Hands shaking the whole way.
The house was unlocked. And empty. Except it wasn't.
Every room matched mine. Same furniture. Same layout. Same scratch on the kitchen counter, in the same place, at the same angle.
My couch. My curtains. Even the chipped mug I keep meaning to throw out, sitting in the sink. Chipped on the same side.
But no clothes in the closets. No food in the fridge. Nobody had ever lived there.
One difference. The calendar on the fridge.
Mine shows this month. This one was three weeks ahead.
And a single date was circled in red. It's this Friday.
I called the county the next morning. The house isn't in any records. The lot is officially registered as empty.
So now I can't decide. This Friday, should I be home... or as far away as possible?
